name: Nationality by Declaration (Marriage to a Burkinabe Citizen)

requirements.blocker_text: Under the new Code des personnes et de la famille (Loi n.012-2025/ALT, September 2025), marriage to a Burkinabe citizen no longer confers nationality automatically -- a major reversal of the prior rule. Article 153-1 requires the foreign or stateless spouse to wait at least 5 years from the marriage before declaring acquisition, with at least 3 years of continuous residence in Burkina Faso during that time, and to maintain a genuine 'communaute de vie tant affective que materielle' (shared emotional and material life) with the Burkinabe spouse throughout. The government retains a 12-month window to formally oppose the acquisition by council decree (Article 155-5). The provision is gender-neutral, applying identically to a foreign husband or foreign wife.
requirements.fix_path: Marry a Burkinabe citizen, maintain the marriage and a genuine shared life for at least 5 years, with at least 3 years of continuous residence in Burkina Faso, then file a declaration of acquisition.

requirements.blocker_text: Article 153-1's alternative track: where the 3-year continuous-residence condition is not met, a total marriage duration of 7 years applies instead before the foreign or stateless spouse can declare acquisition, subject to the same genuine-shared-life requirement and the government's 12-month opposition window.
requirements.fix_path: Maintain the marriage and a genuine shared life for at least 7 years, then file a declaration of acquisition.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of genuine shared life (correspondence, joint accounts, cohabitation records)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 3 years continuous residence (resident track); none required on the 7-year non-resident track

sources.title: Presidence du Faso (Burkina Faso's official presidency website) -- government summary of the new Code des personnes et de la famille's major innovations, confirming the 5-year minimum wait for nationality acquisition by marriage
AFRILEX (University of Bordeaux law journal) -- detailed academic analysis of Article 153-1's 3-year-resident/7-year-non-resident structure and the government's Article 155-5 opposition right
Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative -- reporting on Burkina Faso's tightening of automatic marriage-based nationality, confirming the end of automatic acquisition and the 5-year minimum wait

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Burkina Faso). STATUS: DRAFT -- the resident track's core hard requirement (the 5-year minimum wait, ending automatic acquisition) is confirmed directly by presidencedufaso.bf, Burkina Faso's own presidency website, tier 1; but the non-resident track's 7-year figure is sourced only to a tier-3 academic law journal, and the validator requires EVERY hard requirement in a published route to cite tier 1 -- so the whole file stays draft until a government source for that second track is located. The finer 3-year-resident structure and the government's opposition right are corroborated by two independent tier-3 sources (an academic law journal and a citizenship-rights NGO), giving strong convergent detail even though those specific sub-details are not independently tier-1-confirmed. MAJOR, CURRENT, WELL-DOCUMENTED LEGAL CHANGE -- FLAGGED PROMINENTLY: as of September 2025 (essentially brand new at the time of this build), Burkina Faso abolished automatic citizenship-by-marriage entirely and replaced it with a genuinely demanding declaration process -- a real tightening, not a formality change, and a rare case in this dataset where a country's marriage-citizenship route became MORE restrictive rather than staying static or liberalizing. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING WITHIN THE TIGHTENING: the new rule is explicitly gender-neutral (applies identically regardless of which spouse is the foreigner), unlike several other countries' marriage-citizenship routes built in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed left null: no source reviewed addressed whether the new declared nationality requires renouncing the original one.
